title: Evaluate Division
summary: Each equation row [a,b] states that a divided by b equals the corresponding entry in values.

contractDetails.constraints: 1–20 equations and 1–20 queries, each with two names of 1–5 lowercase English letters or digits. There is one positive ratio per equation, at most 20. Equations are consistent and queries do not require division by zero. Finite outputs are checked with absolute and relative tolerance; the source gives no additional magnitude bound for derived ratios.
contractDetails.output-checking: Serialize finite numeric ratios in query order. Unknown ratios are exactly −1. Use relative tolerance 1e−7 and absolute tolerance 1e−9 for known ratios. The source has no bound on derived magnitudes beyond the input ratio limits.

statement: Each equation row [a,b] states that a divided by b equals the corresponding entry in values. Answer each requested ratio in order. Return −1.0 for an unknown variable or a pair whose ratio cannot be inferred. A known variable divided by itself is 1.0.

examples.explanation: The forward ratios multiply, and reversing the path takes the reciprocal.
Reverse a quarter and check a known self-ratio.
Separate components and unknown variables have no inferred ratio.

hints: Conceptual: A ratio can be reversed by taking its reciprocal.
Directional: Treat known ratios as directed weighted edges.
Implementation: Traverse from the numerator, multiplying edge ratios until the denominator is reached. Reject disconnected or unknown endpoints.
complexityAnalysis: O(q(V+E)) traversal time with adjacency lists, or O(qV²) for the bounded matrix reference, with O(V+E) or O(V²) graph storage respectively. Add logarithms along a path before converting back to a ratio.
